title: pr-checks.yml substitutes a pull request's description into a shell script, so the description runs as code, and three CI steps pass when their own command fails
body:
Found on 2026-09-24 by a verifier dc ran over `.github/workflows/` for the 3.2.1 doc audit, and reproduced by dc the same day against the files at `cc34b16e4`. Filed with its fix, on vc's ruling.

Seen, at `080bb940a` before the fix:

- **Script injection.** The steel-thread check reads the description as `PR_BODY="${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}"` inside `run:` (`pr-checks.yml:30`). Actions substitutes an expression into the script text before bash parses it, so the description becomes shell source. Reproduced with the step's own lines under `bash -e`, the shell a `run:` step gets when it names none:
  - a body carrying `$(echo SUBSTITUTION-RAN 1>&2)` ran the substitution, at rc 0;
  - a body with an unbalanced `"` was a syntax error, at rc 2, whatever the body referenced;
  - a Markdown code span is the same substitution to bash: under `bash -e` (bash 5.3, driven locally rather than on a runner) a body carrying a backticked command ran it and lost the span from the text, at rc 0.

  The workflow runs on `pull_request`, where a run from a fork gets a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and no secrets. That bounds the harm, but within it anyone who can open a pull request runs code in the step. The script's other expressions (`:154-155`) are the additions and deletions counts, integers GitHub computes, and they stay.

- **check-documentation and test-coverage cannot warn.** Both check out at the default depth of 1 (`pr-checks.yml:64` and `:91`, with no `fetch-depth`), unlike commit-message-check (`:117`), so `origin/main` is not a ref in either job. Each pipes `git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD` into `grep` (`:74`, `:78`, `:98`, `:102`) in a shell without `pipefail`, so the failed diff reads as no change and the step passes. Reproduced: at depth 1 both steps passed at rc 0 and neither warned.

- **The prettier install passes without prettier.** rust.yml's step pipes `prettier --version` into `tee` (`rust.yml:143`), so the step's status is tee's, while its comment (`:134-140`) says that line fails the step when the install puts no binary on PATH. Reproduced with npm stubbed and no network: rc 0.

Expected: text a pull request supplies reaches a step through `env:` and is read as a variable, never substituted into the script; a step whose own check fails, fails.

Fixed by the bank that lands with this issue, `refs/bank/dc/audit/ci-9-10` (blob `ffa1e816b`, patch-id `3fa48ac5abc3`):

- the steel-thread step takes the body through `env: PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}`, and the interpolated line is gone;
- check-documentation and test-coverage check out with `fetch-depth: 0`, and each takes `CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD)` first, so a failed diff fails the step;
- the prettier step sets `pipefail`;
- check-documentation's `CHANGED_FILES="${{ github.event.pull_request.changed_files }}"` (`:71`) is deleted: nothing read it, and it was that script's second interpolation.

The red/green reproduction is banked beside it (`ci-9-10-repro.sh`, `8ab0be3b5`; its log, `ea3dc1283`). On the new files neither body runs or breaks the step; at depth 1 both checks fail loudly at rc 128, and on a full fetch they warn; the prettier step fails at rc 127.

Disposition: vc, 2026-09-24. Member 3 of the doc audit's landing composition, in the fix set hv ruled into 3.2.1 on 2026-09-24. A change to the CI configuration owes the whole crate suites and the shell half, which the stacked final-tree run pays, and this issue closes on vc's PASS of that run. The workflows run on GitHub, so the fixed steps first run in the CI of hv's push.
